input: Learn to play chess openings from YouTube tutorials

gold.taskTitle: Learn Chess Openings From YouTube Tutorials
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to study and learn chess openings by watching YouTube tutorials.

questions.title: What is your current chess skill level right now?
questions.description: Understanding whether the user is a complete beginner, casual player, or intermediate will shape which openings and tutorials are appropriate.

questions.title: Which side do you want to learn openings for?
questions.description: Knowing if the user wants to focus on White openings, Black openings, or both helps narrow the scope of tutorials to find.

questions.title: Do you have specific openings in mind to learn?
questions.description: The user may already have target openings such as the Sicilian Defense, Italian Game, or Queen's Gambit, which would focus the search.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Time availability will determine how ambitious the learning plan can be and how to pace the tutorial-watching schedule.

questions.title: Do you prefer a single YouTube channel or multiple sources?
questions.description: Some learners prefer consistency with one teacher's style, while others benefit from diverse perspectives across channels.

questions.title: Will you practice the openings in real games while learning?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user plans to apply openings on a platform like Chess.com or Lichess alongside watching helps structure the plan.

questions.title: What is your target deadline to complete this goal?
questions.description: A specific timeframe or milestone helps build a realistic schedule for watching tutorials and retaining the material.
